notable_defects: Stage icons are small abstract glyphs; the pre-sort (stage 2) and screens (stage 3) icons are hard to decode at full size and become indistinct squiggles at half width, so the pictograms add little explanation
Row 1 is dense: connector labels, callout speech-bubble tails and card edges sit close together, and the contamination callout tail grazes the stage-2/connector zone
Glass callout tail points at stage 3's lower-left corner rather than at the screen mechanism itself; anchoring is correct but loose

No explicit baled-output terminal element: the kerbside-to-baled-output arc ends inside stage 6 (bale pictograms and caption) rather than at a distinct output destination, a weaker reading of the brief's endpoint
Callout leader dots land ~5px below the target panels' bottom edges rather than on them; visually acceptable but geometrically off-panel
Glass callout's broken-jar icon is ambiguous at a glance (reads crown-like); 11px body text at half width is at the legibility floor (as in A)

notes: Both are technically clean: exact 0 0 960 600 viewBox, fully self-contained (system font stacks, internal styles), six grouped stages in a serpentine, labelled connectors, both required callouts correctly anchored, no collisions or clipping at 960px or 480px, and factually sound single-stream MRF explanations. B wins on communication quality: its pictograms actually depict each mechanism (trommel with shards falling into a hopper, eddy-current fling, air-jet eject, picker pulling a bag) with one consistent dashed-arc motion vocabulary, and they stay legible at half width, where A's small abstract glyphs collapse. B also separates annotation from flow more cleanly (dashed leader plus dot versus solid arrows), carries proper ARIA wiring (role=img, aria-labelledby, full-sequence desc), and its DECISIONS.md documents a verifiable render-critique-fix loop whose claims match the artefact. A's genuine edge is the brief's endpoint: its dedicated baled-output strip with a dashed 'glass cullet (loose)' chip completes the kerbside-to-bale arc and visually reinforces the glass callout, which B only handles inside stage 6 and a footer. That edge narrows but does not close the gap created by B's stronger pictograms, hierarchy and accessibility.
